samples.summary: Adding `readOnly` to the editor-mount effect deps is scope creep for a #1045 (undo-unit) PR, and it contradicts the decision the sibling view already records. `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-view.tsx:1222-1228` explicitly documents the opposite stance for the same prop — "`readOnlyMount` is also excluded: it is derived from a share-link role that is fixed for the lifetime of the route, so toggling it at runtime is not a supported scenario" — and `packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:156-157` has the identical `[didMount, doc]` shape with `readOnly` captured once at `initialize(...)` (line 138). After this change the three views give two different answers to the same question: docs tears down and rebuilds the whole editor (new `YorkieDocStore`, lost caret/scroll/selection, re-run of the `ensureTree`/pending-DOCX-import path at lines 354-401) on a permission flip, while slides and notes deliberately do not. Nothing in the diff updates `docs/design/docs/docs-collaboration.md` (which only records `initialize(container, store?, theme?, readOnly?)` at line 444) or the slides comment to reflect the new stance, so the divergence is undocumented. Cost stays inside the codebase (an unrelated behaviour change that will now drift from its twins), hence minor rather than major — but either fix all three or leave docs consistent with the recorded decision.

samples.summary: The new `this.readOnly` re-check in `pastePlainTextFromClipboard()` is justified by a mechanism this design does not have. `readOnly` is a private field assigned only in the constructor (`text-editor.ts:191`, `:719`) with no setter anywhere in `packages/docs/src` (grep for `setReadOnly|readOnly =` finds only the two constructor assignments and `doc-canvas.ts`), so it cannot change "between the keydown and the write" on a live instance — a permission change is applied by rebuilding the editor (the `docs-view.tsx` deps change in this same delta), and the old instance is already caught by the `disposed` check on the same line. The synchronous gate at `text-editor.ts:1096` also returns before the Cmd+Shift+V branch (`:1373-1376`) is ever reached under `readOnly`. Harmless defence-in-depth, but the comment ("the permission this session is allowed to exercise is the one that decides — not the one that held when the shortcut was pressed") records a per-instance mutable-permission model the code does not implement, which is the kind of comment future readers build on.
samples.evidence: text-editor.ts:4255-4261 comment + `if (this.disposed || this.pasting || this.readOnly) return;`; `private readOnly = false;` (191) assigned only at 719.

samples.summary: The incremental-layout invariant is now split across two places in the same closure: `recomputeLayout` unconditionally clears `dirtyBlockIds` (editor.ts:1534) and the `requestLayoutRefresh` lambda reaches back into the host closure to put the set back. An explicit parameter (`recomputeLayout({ keepDirty: true })`) or a named helper would keep "who owns the dirty set" in one place; as written, any future caller of `recomputeLayout` has to know the seam re-establishes the state behind its back. Behaviour is as documented in `docs/design/docs/docs-collaboration.md`, so this is taste, not a defect.
samples.evidence: editor.ts:2545-2549 `const dirty = dirtyBlockIds; recomputeLayout(); dirtyBlockIds = dirty ?? new Set();` against editor.ts:1534 `dirtyBlockIds = undefined;`
